Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — ACME MAP draft and next steps

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the business case and the initial eval scope. Per our discussion, I attached a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (acme_map_v1.xlsx) and a short benchmark spec (benchmark_spec.pdf) that lays out the technical evaluation milestone. Please find the technical-eval section copied below for quick reference.

Technical evaluation milestone (owner: Redwood + ACME engineering) — target completion: 2027-08-12
- Goal: Validate model choice and serving configuration for customer-facing chat assistant.
- Success criteria (pass = all must be true):
  - Quality: >= 85% pass-rate on ACME evaluation rubric (representative prompts + human review sample).
  - Latency: P95 end-to-end response time <= 300 ms for 256-token responses in Redwood Dedicated (us-west).
  - Cost: Estimated per-1M-token inference cost <= $75 under expected traffic profile (batching + caching enabled).
  - Reliability: No more than 1% inference error rate (timeouts/failed responses) during benchmark runs.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1M tokens (hosted and dedicated estimates), inference error rate, qualitative failure modes.
- Model shortlist: LLaMA 3 13B (q4), Mistral Large 7B (float16), Open-7B (baseline), and a distilled 3B candidate for low-cost comparison.
- Test data: ACME will provide a 500-case representative prompt set and 50 human-eval prompts for qualitative review.
- Responsibilities:
  - ACME: deliver anonymized representative prompt set and evaluation rubric by 2027-07-22; provide test credentials for sandbox environment.
  - Redwood: provision Dedicated instances, run automated benchmarks, collect metrics, and produce a benchmark report with recommended configs by 2027-08-12.
- Dependencies: VPC peering or secure upload for test data, short list of endpoints to hit (customer-side rate limits), approval for sample data handling (PII checklist).

Next steps (short):
1) ACME to confirm prompt set and rubric (target: 2027-07-22).
2) Redwood to provision test capacity once credentials/data available and schedule benchmark window (target: 2027-07-25).
3) Redwood delivers benchmark report and recommended model/config (target: 2027-08-12).

I've attached the Excel MAP and the benchmark spec for more detail. If you prefer, we can add or tighten the latency/cost thresholds — happy to iterate based on your priorities.

Best,

- Latency is our top priority for the initial MVP (user-facing chat). Can we tighten the P95 goal to 250 ms if possible, or at least run a subtest that prioritizes latency vs. cost?
- Please add an open-source 7B (we use it in prod today) to the shortlist so we have an apples-to-apples baseline.
- On the dataset: we'll produce the 500-case prompt set but need guidance on how to anonymize PII — can Mateo and your team sync on that?
